qt: to the Commission Giuseppe Antoci (The Left) Subject:

The monetisation of creative activities through digital platforms offers young people professional opportunities, but it can lead to income instability, contractual imbalances, poor pay and unsustainable workloads. Directive (EU) 2024/2831 regulates platform work and algorithmic management, and extends some protections to non-employees1. Its applicability to content creators and digital creative professionals needs to be clarified in the light of Article 22. In Sicily, too, digital opportunities should go hand in hand with quality employment and protection for young people. In the light of the above: 1.

Will the Commission publish guidelines on the applicability of Directive (EU) 2024/2831 to content creators and digital creative professionals, particularly with reference to the requirement that the platform organise the work, and by when?

Has it assessed whether European protections for those professionals are up to scratch, including the protections outside the scope of the directive, with regard to transparency of remuneration criteria, unilateral contract changes and account suspensions? If so, what were the outcomes, measures and timelines? If not, will it carry out an assessment of that kind and within what timeline?

Do European Social Fund Plus (ESF+) measures that support youth employment in Sicily include digital and creative pathways, and what indicators measure the quality of career prospects with regard to contractual conditions, remuneration and social protection?

https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2024/2831/oj/eng, in particular, Articles 1 and 2. Article 31 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union protects workers’ right to working conditions that honour their dignity, to limits on working hours and to rest. https://www.europarl.europa.eu/charter/pdf/text_en.pdf.
